To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

each doubling of SUV max as determined by pre-operative PET is associated with 1.28 fold increase in the hazard of death in patients with early stage NSCLC and preoperative SUV max was not found to be a independent predictor of overall survivals in these patients.

the maximum standardized uptake values (SUVmaxs) of the primary tumors as determined by pre-operative 18F-fluro-2-deoxy-D-glucose positron emission tomographies (18F-FDGPET) are not an independent predictors of overall survival in early-stage non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC).

the maximum standardized uptake (SUVmax ) of the primary tumor on preoperative 18 F-fluoro- 2 -deoxyglucose ( 18 F-FDG ) positron emission tomograph (PET) in patients with early-stage (I and II ) non -small cell lung cancers ( NSCLC ) was not an independent prognostic indicator of overall survival.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prognostic significance of preoperative SUVmax in early-stage NSCLC.
the prognostic significance of SUVmax in early-stage (stage I and stage II) NSCLCs.

the prognostic significance of preoperative ¹⁸F-FDG PET in early-stage (IA and IB) NSCLC and the value of preoperative PET in predicting the overall survival of early-stage (I) NSCLC after surgical resection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SUVmax as determined preoperatively by PET has no value in predicting the overall survival of early-stage (I&II) NSCLC.
the preoperative PET SUVmax is not a reliable prognostic marker in early-stage NSCLC.
preoperative 18FDG-PET SUVmax does not have any prognostic significance in early-stage NSCLC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
preoperative 18-FDG PET has no prognostic value in patients with early-stage (I and II) NSCLCs.

preoperative 18-FDG PET SUVmax is not a reliable predictor of overall survival in early-stage (IA, IB, & IIB) NSCLC, and that the prognostic significance of preoperative PET SUVmax is dependent on the stage of NSCLC.
preoperative PET is not useful in early stage NSCLC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
preoperative PET is not an independent prognostic factor for overall survival in early-stage (IA, IB, and II) non-small-cell lung cancer.
SUVmax is not a useful prognostic marker in early-stage (IA, IB, and II) NSCLCs.
the prognostic significance of preoperative PET in early-stage NSCLC is not stage specific and the prognostic utility of preoperative PET is limited.
